extracted.intended_audience: Wattpad authors / writers publishing fiction on Wattpad
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and applying tags to Wattpad stories to maximize discoverability and correctly label content for appropriate audiences. Covers platform rules, algorithmic factors, and recommended tag types (genre, subgenre, theme, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tags are key to story discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tags ensure your story appears in different locations across Wattpad, from search results to home feeds, and influence placement on the Hot List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the right strategy, you can optimize discoverability by using tags that align with your plot. Popularity, relevance, trendiness, and user engagement are factors that influence tag rankings; Wattpad's algorithm processes a variety of metrics to develop the Hot List.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard and fast rules for tag syntax and count
rubrics_metrics.description: Tags should be one word and they should give the reader an idea of what they might find when reading your story. Stories can have a maximum of 25 tags. Special characters, such as punctuation marks or spaces, cannot be present in tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these constraints exactly: use single-word tags (no spaces), avoid punctuation/special characters, and do not exceed 25 tags. These are platform-enforced rules rather than stylistic suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature rating and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are under the age of 17 and you mark your story as Mature, your rankings will not appear on your profile or on the Hot Lists for ranked tags; readers older than 17 will be able to view rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Mature rating for stories with explicit sex scenes, self-harm themes or scenes, graphic depictions of violence, or other content inappropriate for younger members. The Mature tag protects younger readers but may limit visibility for under-17 authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag the broad genre of your story so readers know what to expect (e.g., #mystery, #fanfic, #scifi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre preferences differ; tagging your genre helps prospective readers decide whether to try your story before committing to a long read. Use the overarching genre(s) that best describe your story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenre tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag specific subgenres beneath the main genre to give more precise signals (e.g., #spies, #dystopian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories are multidimensional—use subgenre tags to capture the specific niche or twist that distinguishes your story from broader genre entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag the unifying thematic threads of your story (e.g., #courage, #comingofage, #redemption, #revenge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the core themes that weave through your tale and include those as tags to attract readers looking for those thematic elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and tag the intended reader demographic (e.g., #youngadult, #mature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging for audience helps readers discover content suited to their preferences and expectations; identify your audience early and reflect it in tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag the emotional tone or mood of your story (e.g., #angsty, #feelgood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help readers gauge the emotional experience they can expect by including mood-based tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and place tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag the story's temporal or geographic setting (e.g., #alternateuniverse, #Paris, #future).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers appreciate knowing when and where a story takes place—use tags that signal setting and setting-related appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wildcards / specific-plot tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag unique or standout elements of your plot that make it distinct (e.g., #queerromance, #volleyball).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider what makes your story unique and use those specific tags to entice niche audiences who might otherwise skip over your story.
